ei.title: Faster, Higher, Stronger: What Innovations Bring
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
Faster, Higher, Stronger: What Innovations Bring

Five sprinters were getting ready at the starting line of the men's 100-meter sprint in 1896 when the first modern Olympic Games were held. One sprinter in particular caught the spectators' attention. He was touching the ground with his hips raised towards the sky, while the others were simply standing. The spectators laughed at the position of his body, but it took only 11.8 seconds for them to witness him setting the first Olympic record. This sprinter's name was Thomas Burke, and his innovative technique called a crouch start has become the standard starting position since then. Here are some key innovations introduced by great athletes who challenged themselves to find what worked best. They proved that there is always room for improvement.

The Flip Turn in Swimming

Up until the 1936 Olympics, swimmers used an open turn. They touched the wall with one or two hands first, turned to the side, and pushed off from the wall by bending their legs. However, open turns had the critical disadvantage of disrupting the swimmers' flow and speed.

This problem was resolved by an American high school student named Al Vande Weghe. While practicing the backstroke, he realized that his legs were too heavy for an open turn, which caused him to slow down. To overcome this drawback, he devised a technique that is now known as a flip turn. He would make a forward roll first to change direction and then kick against the wall to speed ahead. This technique allowed him to maintain as much of his speed and momentum as possible. His willingness to take a risk and keep experimenting paid off. Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the 1936 Olympics. Flip turns are now the standard in freestyle and backstroke races.

The V Style in Ski Jumping

Ski jumping is one of the most spectacular winter Olympic events. The skiers jump from the height of 90 meters, which is as high as a 30-story apartment building. Most of the skiers are able to stay in the air for about five to seven seconds. While they are in the air, they are influenced by "lift," an upward force produced by air on a fast-moving object. When the force of lift is balanced with the force of gravity, the skiers can fly for long distances. The key factors for them to increase lift and jumping distance are increasing their speed, spreading out their bodies and skis, and adjusting their body angle.

As jumps are judged mostly on jumping distance as well as their style, skiers have tried many techniques to maximize their time in the air, aiming to achieve longer distances. In the beginning, most skiers simply stood upright throughout their jump. Later, this upright style was replaced by the Kongsberger style. The skiers' upper body was bent at the hips, with their arms extended in front of them and their skis parallel to each other. This technique doubled the average jumping distance.

Everything changed in 1985, however, when Swedish jumper Jan Boklöv introduced the V style. In this style, the skiers position their skis into a "V" shape with their heads placed between the skis. This modification increases the surface area and creates more lift, leading to even greater jumping distances. Wind tunnel tests showed that the V style improves air lift by 28%, which means that skiers can stay in the air longer. This style also enables skiers to land at a safer speed, reducing the risk of injury.

The V style was not immediately adopted by the skiing community. In fact, it was initially ridiculed and received few style points for breaking the standard of parallel skis. However, the technique proved so successful that by 1992 all Olympic medalists were using it.

The Fosbury Flop in High Jumping

Dick Fosbury practiced the major high jump techniques, such as the scissors and the straddle, for the Olympics when he was in high school. He soon realized, however, that these techniques were challenging for him because he didn't have the strength or speed they require. Then he found that when he went over the bar backward and landed headfirst, he could jump higher than anyone on his team. As an engineering major, he later explained that arching the body backward keeps the jumper's center of gravity low to the ground. The lower the center of gravity, the less energy required to successfully jump over the bar. Another advantage is that with this technique, there is less chance that the jumper's arms or legs will hit the bar and knock it down.

The result was a huge success. Fosbury won a gold medal in the high jump in the 1968 Olympics. But up to that point, every jumper in the event had only gone over the bar forward, not backward. Local newspapers criticized his style, saying that he looked like "a fish flopping in a boat" and calling him "the world's laziest high jumper." Eight years later, however, 90% of all high jumpers were going over the bar backward just like Fosbury. Today, every high jumper performs what is known as the "Fosbury Flop."

Athletes often face challenges when they realize that conventional techniques aren't working out for them. They then make determined efforts to overcome these weaknesses. Some of these athletes end up developing remarkable innovative techniques, which eventually become the new norm. Innovation flourishes when individuals have a deep understanding of themselves and discover their own unique strengths.

questions.passage: One sprinter in particular caught the spectators' attention. He was touching the ground with his hips raised towards the sky, while the others were simply standing. The spectators laughed at the position of his body, but it took only 11. 8 seconds for them to witness him setting the first Olympic record. This sprinter's name was Thomas Burke, and his (A)[innovative / conventional] technique called a crouch start has become the (B)[temporary / standard] starting position since then. Here are some key innovations introduced by great athletes who (C)[challenged / discouraged] themselves to find what worked best. They proved that there is always room for improvement.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그의 혁신적인(innovative) 기법인 크라우치 스타트는 표준(standard) 출발 자세가 되었고, 위대한 선수들이 스스로에게 도전했다(challenged).
det.analysis:
✅ ② innovative — standard — challenged: 원문 일치. 크라우치 스타트는 '혁신적(innovative)' 기법이고, '표준(standard)' 자세가 되었으며, 선수들이 스스로에게 '도전했다(challenged)'.
❌ ① conventional(관습적인): 새로운 기법이므로 innovative가 맞음
❌ ③ temporary(임시적인): 지금까지 이어지는 표준이므로 standard가 맞음
❌ ④ discouraged(낙담시킨): 최선을 찾기 위해 도전했으므로 challenged가 맞음
det.tip: innovative(혁신적인) ↔ conventional(관습적인). standard(표준적인) ↔ temporary(임시적인).

questions.passage: While practicing the backstroke, he realized that his legs were too heavy for an open turn, which caused him to slow down. To (A)[overlook / overcome] this drawback, he (B)[devised / abandoned] a technique that is now known as a flip turn. He would make a forward roll first to change direction and then kick against the wall to speed ahead. This technique allowed him to (C)[maintain / sacrifice] as much of his speed and momentum as possible. His willingness to take a risk and keep experimenting paid off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 단점을 극복하기(overcome) 위해, 그는 플립턴이라 알려진 기술을 고안했다(devised). 이 기술 덕분에 속도와 운동량을 최대한 유지할(maintain) 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ overcome — devised — maintain: 원문 일치
❌ ① overlook(간과하다): 단점을 '극복'한 것이지 '간과'한 것이 아님
❌ ② abandoned(포기하다): 기술을 '고안'한 것이지 '포기'한 것이 아님
❌ ④ sacrifice(희생하다): 속도를 '유지'한 것이지 '희생'한 것이 아님
det.tip: overcome(극복하다) ↔ overlook(간과하다). devise(고안하다) ↔ abandon(포기하다). maintain(유지하다) ↔ sacrifice(희생하다).

questions.passage: Wind tunnel tests showed that the V style improves air lift by 28%, which means that skiers can stay in the air longer. This style also enables skiers to land at a safer speed, reducing the risk of injury. The V style was not immediately (A)[adopted / imposed] by the skiing community. In fact, it was initially (B)[celebrated / ridiculed] and received few style points for breaking the standard of parallel skis. However, the technique proved so (C)[successful / controversial] that by 1992 all Olympic medalists were using it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: V 스타일은 스키 커뮤니티에 즉시 채택되지(adopted) 않았다. 사실 처음에는 조롱받았고(ridiculed), 그러나 그 기술이 매우 성공적이어서(successful) 1992년에는 모든 메달리스트가 사용했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ adopted — ridiculed — successful: 원문 일치
❌ ① imposed(부과하다, 강제하다): '즉시 채택되지 않았다'이므로 adopted가 맞음. imposed는 강제의 뜻으로 문맥과 다름
❌ ② celebrated(찬양하다): '처음에 조롱받았다'이므로 ridiculed가 맞음
❌ ③ controversial(논란이 되는): '매우 성공적'이므로 successful이 맞음
det.tip: adopt(채택하다) ≠ impose(부과하다). ridicule(조롱하다) ↔ celebrate(찬양하다). successful(성공적인) ↔ controversial(논란이 되는).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 기술 덕분에 속도와 운동량(momentum)을 최대한 유지할 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ momentum(운동량): 'speed and ____'에서 speed와 함께 유지해야 할 물리적 개념. 'as much of his speed and momentum as possible'이 원문
❌ ① direction(방향): speed and direction은 가능하나 원문과 다름
❌ ② balance(균형): 속도 유지 맥락에서 'speed and balance'는 부자연스러움
❌ ③ position(위치): 'speed and position'은 의미상 부적합
det.tip: momentum(운동량): 물체가 가진 운동의 양. speed(속도)와 함께 쓰이는 핵심 물리 개념.

det.korean: 양력과 중력(gravity)의 힘이 균형을 이루면 스키 선수는 먼 거리를 날 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① gravity(중력): 'lift(양력)'과 대비되는 힘으로 'balanced with the force of ____'에 가장 적합
❌ ② pressure(압력): lift와 직접 대비되는 힘이 아님
❌ ③ friction(마찰력): 공중 비행 맥락에서 주요 대비 힘이 아님
❌ ④ velocity(속도): 힘(force)이 아닌 운동 상태를 나타내는 말
det.tip: lift(양력) ↔ gravity(중력). 스키점프에서 양력이 중력과 균형을 이루면 비행 가능.

det.korean: 사실 처음에는 조롱받았고(ridiculed) 평행 스키 기준을 깨트렸다는 이유로 스타일 점수도 낮았다.

❌ ② imitated(모방했다): 나중에야 모방됨. 처음에는 조롱
❌ ③ ignored(무시했다): 무시가 아닌 적극적 조롱

questions.passage: As an engineering major, he later explained that arching the body backward keeps the jumper's center of gravity low to the ground. The lower the center of gravity, the less energy required to successfully jump over the bar. Another <u>advantage</u> is that with this technique, there is less chance that the jumper's arms or legs will hit the bar and knock it down.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 advantage와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 또 다른 장점(advantage)은 선수의 팔이나 다리가 바를 칠 가능성이 적다는 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ drawback(단점): advantage(장점)의 반의어. 같은 글에서 flip turn의 'drawback'도 등장
❌ ① benefit(이점): advantage의 동의어
❌ ② feature(특징): 중립적 단어, 반의어 아님
❌ ④ strength(강점): advantage의 유의어
det.tip: advantage(장점) ↔ drawback/disadvantage(단점). benefit ≈ advantage ≈ strength.

questions.passage:
"

Athletes often face challenges when they realize that <u>conventional</u> techniques aren't working out for them. They then make determined efforts to overcome these weaknesses. Some of these athletes end up developing remarkable innovative techniques, which eventually become the new norm. Innovation flourishes when individuals have a deep understanding of themselves and discover their own unique strengths.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 conventional과 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 선수들은 전통적인(conventional) 기술이 통하지 않을 때 도전에 직면한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② innovative(혁신적인): conventional(전통적인, 관습적인)의 정반대. 이 글의 핵심 주제가 혁신 vs 전통
❌ ① traditional(전통적인): conventional의 동의어
❌ ③ familiar(익숙한): conventional과 유사한 의미
❌ ④ standard(표준적인): conventional과 유사한 의미
det.tip: conventional = traditional = standard(전통적인) ↔ innovative = creative = novel(혁신적인).

questions.passage:
(A) The spectators laughed at the <u>position</u> of his body, but it took only 11.8 seconds for them to witness him setting the first Olympic record.

(B) After years of hard work, she finally got a management <u>position</u> at a leading company.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 position의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 관중은 그의 몸의 자세(position)를 보고 웃었다. (B) 수년간 노력 끝에 주요 기업의 관리직 직위(position)를 얻었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ (A) 자세 — (B) 직위:

(A) 'the position of his body'에서 position은 몸의 '자세/포즈'. 크라우치 스타트 자세를 보고 관중이 웃은 것.

(B) 'a management position'에서 position은 회사에서의 '직위/직책'.

❌ ① (A) 위치: '몸의 위치'보다 '몸의 자세'가 더 정확
❌ ② (B) 위치: management position은 '관리직 직위'
❌ ③ (B) 입장: '입장(stance)'은 의견/태도이며 직업 맥락과 안 맞음
det.tip: position: ① 자세(body position) ② 위치(location) ③ 직위(job position) ④ 입장(stance)

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

a method or way of doing something, especially one that involves practical skill

det.korean: 어떤 일을 하는 방법, 특히 실용적 기술을 수반하는 것 → 기법(technique)
det.analysis:
✅ ① technique(기법, 기술): 영영풀이 'a method or way of doing something'에 정확히 부합. 이 글에서 crouch start, flip turn, V style 등이 모두 technique
❌ ② momentum(운동량): 물리학 개념, 방법이 아님
❌ ③ gravity(중력): 자연의 힘, 방법이 아님
❌ ④ advantage(장점): 이점/유리함, 방법이 아님
det.tip: technique = a method involving practical skill. 이 글에서 crouch start, flip turn, V style, Fosbury Flop 모두 technique.

questions.passage: His __________ (willing) to take a risk and keep experimenting paid off. Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the 1936 Olympics.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 알맞은 형태를 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 위험을 감수하고 계속 실험하려는 그의 의지(willingness)가 결실을 맺었다.
det.analysis: willing(형용사: 기꺼이 ~하는) → willingness(명사: 의지, 기꺼이 함). 빈칸 앞 소유격 'His'가 명사를 요구하므로 명사형 willingness가 정답.
det.tip: willing(adj.) → willingness(n.). -ness 접미사: 형용사 → 명사 (happy → happiness, kind → kindness).

overlay.excerptSentences: His __________ (willing) to take a risk and keep experimenting paid off. Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the 1936 Olympics.

questions.passage: This __________ (modify) increases the surface area and creates more lift, leading to even greater jumping distances.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 알맞은 형태를 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 이 변형(modification)은 표면적을 늘려 더 많은 양력을 만들어 점프 거리를 더 늘렸다.
det.analysis: modify(동사: 수정하다, 변형하다) → modification(명사: 변형, 수정). 빈칸 앞 지시대명사 'This'와 뒤 동사 'increases'가 주어 명사를 요구하므로 modification이 정답.
det.tip: modify(v.) → modification(n.). -ify 동사의 명사형: modify → modification, identify → identification, simplify → simplification.

overlay.excerptSentences: This __________ (modify) increases the surface area and creates more lift, leading to even greater jumping distances.

questions.passage: This technique allowed him to maintain as much of his speed and momentum as possible. His willingness to take a risk and keep __________ paid off. Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the 1936 Olympics. Flip turns are now the standard in freestyle and backstroke races.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 위험을 감수하고 계속 실험하려는(experimenting) 의지가 결실을 맺었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② experimenting(실험하는): 새로운 기술(플립턴)을 시도하고 발전시킨 맥락. 'take a risk and keep experimenting'은 혁신 과정
❌ ① competing(경쟁하는): 경쟁이 아닌 새 기술 개발 맥락
❌ ③ performing(수행하는): 기술 개발 과정이므로 부적합
❌ ④ complaining(불평하는): 문맥과 완전히 반대
det.tip: experiment(실험하다): try new methods. 'take a risk and keep experimenting' = 위험을 감수하고 계속 실험하다.

questions.passage:
"

Athletes often face challenges when they realize that conventional techniques aren't working out for them. They then make determined efforts to overcome these weaknesses. Some of these athletes end up developing remarkable innovative techniques, which eventually become the new norm. Innovation __________ when individuals have a deep understanding of themselves and discover their own unique strengths.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 혁신은 개인이 자기 자신을 깊이 이해하고 고유한 강점을 발견할 때 번성한다(flourishes).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ flourishes(번성하다): 글 전체가 혁신의 성공 사례이므로 결론에서 혁신이 '번성한다'가 적합
❌ ① diminishes(줄어들다): 글의 긍정적 결론과 모순
❌ ② struggles(고군분투하다): 부정적 의미로 결론과 맞지 않음
❌ ④ ceases(멈추다): 글의 결론과 완전히 반대
det.tip: flourish(번성하다, 번창하다) = thrive = prosper. 'Innovation flourishes when...' = 혁신은 ~할 때 번성한다.
